instruction:
You write tests/planner/judges.examples.test.ts only. Import cutJudges (and judgeTarget if you use it) from "../../src/planner/judges.js", TYPESCRIPT and PYTHON from "../../src/language/profiles.js", fixture and fixtureJson from "../helpers.js", loadContour and loadMap from "../../src/contour/load.js", types with `import type`. Build the typed record and map with the harness skeleton of section 2.1 verbatim (record(), contourMap(), REC, MAP, LEDGER, STORE, EMPTY_MAP). Build the six Cut Cards from the cut fixtures with the CUTS skeleton of section 2.1 verbatim (fns, cut, CUTS); Cut Judges 4 wraps each card of fixtureJson("planner/extras.cards.json") as Card[] into {card, component: null, profile: null, functions: [], slicedByMap: true}. One test(...) per example below, in this order, named "<Function> example <n>: <what>"; then at most 8 of your own on section 2.2 rows. Typing traps (section 2.3): every result is a union, so compare it whole with toStrictEqual or narrow before a field (`r.ok ? r.cuts : r.error`); fixtureJson returns unknown: pass it straight into toStrictEqual, cast only to read a field. No vi.mock, vi.stubGlobal, vi.useFakeTimers, no timer, no function or variable named fetch or Fake*. Import only what you use; eslint rejects an unused import and a `let` never reassigned; import test and expect from "vitest".

The examples below are the criterion, and you are its independent author: write one test per example (no fewer, no merging), and each test's docstring names the Function and the example number, e.g. `Cut Judges example 1`.

Examples of Function Cut Judges:
1. given the Cut Cards of Components ledger then store (the map, docs ["docs/TASK.md"]); defaultProfile typescript; hasFile true only for "tests/helpers.ts"; when cutJudges; then the cards equal ledger.judges.json: parse-judge, checks-judge, format-report-judge, ledger-cli-judge, save-ledger-judge, load-ledger-judge (ref: tests/fixtures/planner/ledger.judges.json (the six judges))
2. given the same; the judge checks-judge; when cutJudges; then contextSlice ["docs/TASK.md", "src/ledger/checks.ts", "tests/helpers.ts"]; maxTokens 19000 (3 examples); its instruction holds "Callee Parse Entry: One line of text into an Entry.\nBehaviour: Splits \"<name> <cents>\" at the last space; the cents are digits." and ends "Preconditions a test's setup depends on:\n- ledger · Sum Entries · every line is parsed first, else Parse Entry faults before the sum\n- store · Save Ledger · the directory exists, else the write faults"
3. given the same; the judges parse-judge and ledger-cli-judge (both overridden) and save-ledger-judge (python); when cutJudges; then parse-judge dependsOn ["parse", "checks"], contextSlice ["docs/TASK.md"], maxTokens 30000, target "tests/ledger/parse.examples.test.ts"; ledger-cli-judge instruction exactly "Write the CLI tests." (an Interface card has no examples); save-ledger-judge target "tests/test_save_ledger_examples.py", contextSlice ["docs/TASK.md", "store/save_ledger.py"] (no tests/conftest.py)
4. given the three extra cards of the map as Cut Cards (store-schema → store/schema.py, notes → docs/NOTES.md, ledger-types → src/ledger/types.ts); hasFile always false; when cutJudges; then the cards equal extras.judges.json: store-schema-judge (python by extension, target "tests/test_schema_examples.py", maxTokens 16000) and ledger-types-judge; notes has no code target and no judge (ref: tests/fixtures/planner/extras.cards.json (the cards), tests/fixtures/planner/extras.judges.json (the two judges))

You write tests/planner/plan.examples.test.ts only. Import orderDeck and planSpec from "../../src/planner/plan.js", loadDeck from "../../src/cards/model.js", fixture and fixtureJson from "../helpers.js", loadContour and loadMap from "../../src/contour/load.js", types with `import type`. Build the typed record and map with the harness skeleton of section 2.1 verbatim (record(), contourMap(), REC, MAP, LEDGER, STORE, EMPTY_MAP). Order Deck builds its cards with the card(id, dependsOn) helper of section 2.1 (loadDeck rejects a cycle, F4); Plan Spec 1 compares the cards' {customId, dependsOn}, the generations and externalDependsOn with fixtureJson("planner/ledger.golden.json") and the whole plan with ledger.plan.json; Plan Spec 5 reads record("../../contour.yaml") and contourMap("../../morph-map.json"). One test(...) per example below, in this order, named "<Function> example <n>: <what>"; then at most 8 of your own on section 2.2 rows. Typing traps (section 2.3): every result is a union, so compare it whole with toStrictEqual or narrow before a field (`r.ok ? r.cuts : r.error`); fixtureJson returns unknown: pass it straight into toStrictEqual, cast only to read a field. No vi.mock, vi.stubGlobal, vi.useFakeTimers, no timer, no function or variable named fetch or Fake*. Import only what you use; eslint rejects an unused import and a `let` never reassigned; import test and expect from "vitest".

The examples below are the criterion, and you are its independent author: write one test per example (no fewer, no merging), and each test's docstring names the Function and the example number, e.g. `Order Deck example 1`.

Examples of Function Order Deck:
1. given the cards of the layered deck fixture in reverse order (d, c, b, a); when orderDeck; then {ok: true} with card ids ["a", "b", "c", "d"], generations [["a"], ["b", "c"], ["d"]], externalDependsOn {} (ref: tests/fixtures/decks/layered.json)
2. given cards z (dependsOn ["y", "ext"]), y (none), x (dependsOn ["ext2", "y"]); when orderDeck; then ids ["y", "x", "z"]; generations [["y"], ["x", "z"]]; externalDependsOn {x: ["ext2"], z: ["ext"]}, x first
3. given cards a (dependsOn ["b"]), b (dependsOn ["a"]), c (none); when orderDeck; then {ok: false, error: "dependency cycle among a, b"}

Examples of Function Plan Spec:
1. given the ledger record and map, spec "ledger.yaml", components ["ledger", "store"], judge true, hasFile true only for "tests/helpers.ts"; when planSpec; then ok; card ids with their dependsOn, generations and externalDependsOn equal ledger.golden.json's (17 cards, 5 generations, {"format-report": ["outside"]}); the whole plan equals ledger.plan.json; no slice holds "ledger.yaml" (ref: tests/fixtures/planner/ledger.golden.json (the old mrph's ids, dependsOn, generations, external), tests/fixtures/planner/ledger.plan.json (the whole plan))
2. given the same, components ["store"], judge false; when planSpec; then card ids ["load-ledger", "notes", "save-ledger", "store-schema"], generations [["load-ledger", "notes", "save-ledger", "store-schema"]], externalDependsOn {notes: ["parse"], "save-ledger": ["format-report"]}; save-ledger's slice ["docs/TASK.md"]; ledger-types (Component Ledger) skipped
3. given the ledger map with the parse-entry override's contextSlice ["ledger.yaml", "docs/A.md"]; components ["ledger"], judge false; when planSpec; then the card parse has contextSlice ["docs/A.md"]
4. given the map with language "cobol"; components ["nope"]; an extra card store-schema with component "Nowhere"; an extra card ledger-types renamed "parse"; the parse-entry override with dependsOn ["checks"] (components ["ledger"], judge false); when planSpec; then errors "the map: unknown language 'cobol' (known: typescript, python)"; "no Component 'nope' in the record (have: ledger, store)"; "extra card 'store-schema' names Component 'Nowhere' the record does not have (have: ledger, store)"; "duplicate customId 'parse'"; "dependency cycle among checks, format-report, ledger-cli, notes, parse"
5. given this repository's own contour.yaml and morph-map.json, spec "contour.yaml", components ["contour"], judge true; when planSpec; then generations [["validate-record"], ["select-components", "validate-map", "validate-record-judge"], ["load-spec", "select-components-judge", "validate-map-judge"], ["load-spec-judge"]] — the P9 deck old mrph cut; each card's acceptance is the map's for its id
